phases.name: Walking Skeleton: trend store + delta wiring

steps.name: Rename history store to trends.json and extend HistoryEntry schema
steps.description: Add branch and schema_version fields to HistoryEntry in scorer.rs (both with #[serde(default)] for backward compat). Rename HISTORY_FILE constant from 'history.json' to 'trends.json' in cache/history.rs. Emit the message 'Trend: first snapshot recorded' in renderer/cli.rs when the loaded history slice passed to the renderer is empty.
steps.criteria: Running barad-dur analyze on a repo with no prior .barad-dur/trends.json creates the file at that path (not history.json). The CLI output contains the line 'Trend: first snapshot recorded'. Existing deserialized HistoryEntry values without branch or schema_version fields do not cause a parse error.
quality_gates: trends.json file is created on first run
steps.implementation_notes: Use #[serde(default)] on both new fields so existing NDJSON lines deserialize cleanly. The branch value comes from AnalysisReport.branch which is already populated. schema_version hardcodes to 1. The first-run message check in cli renderer compares the prior_history slice length to zero before rendering the score block.
deliverables: HistoryEntry struct gains branch: String and schema_version: u32 fields
HISTORY_FILE constant is 'trends.json'
CLI renderer emits first-run message when prior history is empty

steps.name: Wire history recording in main.rs with branch-aware dedup
steps.description: Ensure main.rs passes the current branch into build_history_entry and that append_if_new_head correctly deduplicates by SHA. The branch field populated in step 01-01 must flow through the record path so the stored entry carries branch information from the first write.
steps.criteria: Running barad-dur analyze twice on the same commit SHA appends exactly one entry to trends.json. Running it on a second commit SHA appends a second entry. The branch field in each stored NDJSON entry matches the actual git branch of the analyzed repo.
quality_gates: trends.json contains exactly 1 entry after two runs on the same HEAD
trends.json contains 2 entries after runs on two distinct HEADs
steps.implementation_notes: build_history_entry already exists in scorer.rs; the branch value is already on AnalysisReport.branch so it just needs to be assigned to the new field. The dedup logic in append_if_new_head compares last stored head to current head — no branch logic needed in dedup, branch is metadata only.
deliverables: build_history_entry assigns branch from AnalysisReport
append_if_new_head dedup by SHA continues to work with new struct shape

steps.name: Create src/trend.rs with compute_trend() and extend CLI renderer with delta + sparkline
steps.description: Create the new pure-computation module src/trend.rs. Define TrendSummary, TrendDelta, SparklinePoint, and TrendVelocity types. Implement compute_trend(current_score, prior_history) -> TrendSummary with no I/O and no imports from cache/ or renderer/. Extend renderer/cli.rs to call compute_trend and inject a delta line (e.g., '+3 vs last run') and a direction indicator after the overall score line. Extend renderer/json.rs and update relevant main.rs call sites to accept the new TrendSummary.
steps.criteria: When a prior trends.json entry exists for the same branch, the CLI output contains a delta marker on the same line or immediately after the overall score (e.g., '72/100  (+3 vs last run)'). The direction word (improving / declining / stable) appears in CLI output. src/trend.rs imports nothing from src/cache/ or src/renderer/.
quality_gates: trend.rs has zero imports from cache:: or renderer::
No existing json or html renderer tests regress
steps.implementation_notes: TrendSummary is the output of compute_trend. TrendDelta holds delta_vs_last and delta_vs_oldest (i32). SparklinePoint holds (timestamp, score). TrendVelocity holds velocity_per_week (Option<f64>). compute_trend filters history to same-branch entries before computing. The CLI renderer receives a Option<TrendSummary> — None when no prior entries exist.
deliverables: src/trend.rs module with all four types and compute_trend function
CLI renderer shows delta and direction indicator
main.rs wires compute_trend between history load and render call

phases.name: Release 1 Core: full US-01 and US-02 acceptance coverage

steps.name: Verify first-run message exact text and CLI position
steps.description: Ensure the first-run message emitted by cli renderer is exactly the string 'Trend: first snapshot recorded' (case and punctuation must match) and that it appears after the score block, not before it. Adjust renderer/cli.rs output ordering if needed.
steps.criteria: CLI output from a first-run analysis contains the exact string 'Trend: first snapshot recorded'. The string does not appear before the overall score line. Subsequent runs on the same HEAD do not emit the message.
quality_gates: Exact string match confirmed in test assertion
steps.implementation_notes: This is a positioning and wording fix on top of 01-01. The message string must be a named constant to avoid typo drift. Confirm the test seeds an empty trends.json directory and checks stdout.
deliverables: Named constant FIRST_RUN_MESSAGE = 'Trend: first snapshot recorded'
Message positioned after score block in CLI output

steps.name: Archive-and-replace corrupt trends.json with warning
steps.description: Implement maybe_archive_if_corrupt() in cache/history.rs. When load_history encounters a parse error on any line, it archives the existing trends.json to trends.json.bak.{timestamp} and starts a fresh file. Emit a warning to stderr: 'Warning: trends file was corrupt and has been archived to {path}'.
steps.criteria: When trends.json contains invalid JSON on any line, the next run does not error out. The old file is renamed to a timestamped .bak path. A warning is printed to stderr. The new trends.json is written fresh with the current run's entry only.
quality_gates: No panic or process exit code != 0 on corrupt input
Archive file present after corrupt-file run
steps.implementation_notes: maybe_archive_if_corrupt is called inside load_history when serde_json returns an error. The archive filename uses the Unix timestamp to avoid collision. The existing append_if_new_head path is unchanged — it writes to the fresh (now-empty) trends.json.
deliverables: maybe_archive_if_corrupt() function in cache/history.rs
Timestamped .bak archive created on corrupt file
Warning emitted to stderr with archive path

steps.name: Trend recording is not skipped when --no-cache flag is set
steps.description: Confirm that the trend recording path in main.rs (the append_if_new_head call) executes regardless of the --no-cache flag. The --no-cache flag skips the snapshot cache, not the trend store. No code change may be needed; this step validates the existing wiring and adds a guard comment if the two paths could diverge.
steps.criteria: Running barad-dur analyze . --no-cache on a repo with an existing trends.json appends a new entry when the HEAD is new. The --no-cache flag does not prevent trends.json from being updated.
quality_gates: trends.json entry count increases after --no-cache run with new HEAD
steps.implementation_notes: Inspect main.rs flow: snapshot caching branches around lines 89-130, but history recording is at lines 154-157, after the branch. If the recording is already unconditional, this step adds only a comment and a test. If a conditional exists, remove it.
deliverables: Confirmed trend recording is unconditional with respect to --no-cache
Explanatory comment added near recording site in main.rs

steps.name: Document that trend recording makes no additional git calls
steps.description: Verify via test instrumentation (timing, call counts) that the trend recording path (compute_trend + append_if_new_head) does not invoke any git subprocess. Document this guarantee in a comment in trend.rs. The test measures wall-clock overhead in a tight loop and asserts it remains below 500ms.
steps.criteria: A test running compute_trend 1000 times with a 50-entry history slice completes in under 500ms total. trend.rs contains no calls to std::process::Command. The trend recording overhead measured end-to-end is below 500ms as asserted in the test.
quality_gates: Timing assertion passes on CI hardware
steps.implementation_notes: compute_trend is pure (no I/O), so the performance test is a microbenchmark in integration test style. The 500ms budget is generous for pure computation; the test primarily documents the constraint. Use std::time::Instant for measurement.
deliverables: Performance comment in trend.rs documenting the no-git-calls guarantee
Timing assertion in test confirms sub-500ms for 1000 iterations

steps.name: Delta shown inline with overall score in exact format
steps.description: Ensure the overall score line in CLI output matches the exact format 'N/100  (+M vs last run)' for positive delta or 'N/100  (-M vs last run)' for negative delta. Two spaces before the parenthesized delta. The delta is an absolute integer (no decimal places).
steps.criteria: When a prior trends.json entry exists with a different score, CLI stdout contains a line matching the regex '\d+/100  \([+-]\d+ vs last run\)'. The sign is + when current score > prior score, - when lower. When scores are equal, '(+0 vs last run)' or '(stable)' per the direction logic in 02-07.
quality_gates: Regex match on exact output format confirmed
steps.implementation_notes: This step enforces the exact format string. The renderer must format the delta as a signed integer. The two-space separator before '(' is load-bearing for script-compatibility (see 03-01). Align with the TrendDelta.delta_vs_last field from trend.rs.
deliverables: Score line format: 'N/100  (+M vs last run)' exactly
Positive and negative delta cases both covered

steps.name: Per-category deltas shown for all four categories
steps.description: Extend the CLI renderer so that each of the four category score rows (Health, Team, Evolution, Git Hygiene) displays a numeric delta marker alongside the category score. The delta compares the current category score to the last recorded score for the same category on the same branch.
steps.criteria: CLI output contains four category rows each with a delta marker. The marker format is consistent with the overall score format (e.g., '+2' or '-1'). When no prior entry exists for a category, no delta marker is shown for that category.
quality_gates: All four category rows contain delta markers when prior history exists
steps.implementation_notes: TrendSummary should carry a HashMap<String, i32> for per-category deltas. compute_trend builds this map from the last HistoryEntry categories field. The cli renderer iterates categories and appends the delta if present in the map.
deliverables: TrendSummary gains per_category_deltas: HashMap<String, i32>
CLI renderer appends category delta to each category row

steps.name: Sparkline and direction indicator in CLI output
steps.description: Add a trend direction word (improving / declining / stable) and a sparkline character sequence to the CLI output. The direction is derived from the delta_vs_last field: positive = improving, negative = declining, zero = stable. The sparkline is a sequence of Unicode block characters (e.g., '▁▂▄▆█') representing the last N score values.
steps.criteria: CLI output contains one of the words 'improving', 'declining', or 'stable'. CLI output contains a sparkline indicator made of block characters representing recent scores. Both appear only when prior history exists.
quality_gates: Direction word present in output when prior history exists
steps.implementation_notes: Direction is a TrendDirection enum (Improving | Declining | Stable) in trend.rs, serialized to lowercase string. Sparkline renders the last 8 SparklinePoint values using 8 Unicode block characters (U+2581 through U+2588). Map score 0-100 to 8 buckets. Both fields live on TrendSummary.
deliverables: TrendDirection enum with Display impl
Sparkline renderer in trend.rs as pure function
CLI renderer outputs direction and sparkline on separate line

steps.name: Branch mismatch suppresses delta and emits warning
steps.description: When the most recent trends.json entry was recorded on a different branch than the current run, compute_trend must return None (or a TrendSummary with delta suppressed), and the CLI renderer must emit a warning: 'Trend: prior snapshot is from a different branch — delta suppressed'. No delta or sparkline is shown in the score output.
steps.criteria: When trends.json contains entries from branch 'main' and the current run is on branch 'feature/x', CLI output contains the warning 'Trend: prior snapshot is from a different branch — delta suppressed'. No delta marker appears in the overall score line. No sparkline appears in output.
quality_gates: No delta marker in output on branch mismatch
Warning string appears exactly once in stderr or stdout
steps.implementation_notes: compute_trend filters prior history to same-branch entries. If the filtered slice is empty but the unfiltered slice is non-empty, return a BranchMismatch variant or set a flag on TrendSummary. The CLI renderer checks this flag and emits the warning instead of the delta block.
deliverables: compute_trend detects and signals branch mismatch
CLI renderer emits exact warning text on mismatch
Delta and sparkline absent from output on mismatch

phases.name: Release 1 JSON: US-04 JSON trend schema

steps.name: Score line format is backward-compatible when trend delta is shown
steps.description: Verify that the pattern 'N/100' remains present and parseable in CLI output even when the trend delta suffix is appended. Scripts that grep for '\d+/100' must continue to match. The delta suffix must be appended after the existing score token, not replace it.
steps.criteria: CLI output line containing the overall score still matches the regex '\d+/100' when trend delta is shown. The full line reads 'N/100  (+M vs last run)' — the N/100 substring is intact. Running grep '\d+/100' on the output returns at least one line.
quality_gates: Regex '\d+/100' matches output line with delta suffix
steps.implementation_notes: This is a format contract test. No code change expected if 02-05 was implemented correctly. The test constructs output with a seeded prior entry and asserts the regex. Document the format as a stability guarantee in a comment in renderer/cli.rs.
deliverables: Format stability comment in cli renderer
Test confirms backward-compat regex match

steps.name: Add --trend flag to CLI; gate trend key injection in JSON renderer
steps.description: Add a --trend boolean flag to AnalyzeArgs in cli.rs. When --json is used without --trend, the JSON output must contain no 'trend' key — the structure is identical to pre-feature output. When --trend is set alongside --json, the trend key is injected by renderer/json.rs.
steps.criteria: Running barad-dur analyze . --json produces JSON with no 'trend' key. Running barad-dur analyze . --json --trend produces JSON with a 'trend' key. The JSON schema for the non-trend case is byte-for-byte identical to pre-feature output (no new keys, no reordering).
quality_gates: jq '.trend // empty' returns empty for --json without --trend
steps.implementation_notes: The --trend flag is on AnalyzeArgs (cli.rs). It is passed through run_analysis to the json renderer as a separate parameter, not as a field on AnalysisReport (NFR-03 forbids struct modification). The renderer conditionally builds and injects the trend object.
deliverables: --trend flag added to AnalyzeArgs
JSON renderer conditionally injects trend key
No-trend JSON output structurally unchanged

steps.name: velocity_per_week is JSON null when fewer than 2 prior snapshots
steps.description: When --json --trend is used and there is fewer than 2 prior snapshots in trends.json for the current branch, the trend.velocity_per_week field must be present in the JSON output with a null value (key present, value null — not absent).
steps.criteria: With 0 or 1 prior entries in trends.json, running --json --trend produces output where jq '.trend.velocity_per_week' returns 'null' (not an error). With 2+ prior entries, the field is a number.
quality_gates: jq '.trend.velocity_per_week' is numeric with 2+ prior entries
steps.implementation_notes: TrendVelocity.velocity_per_week is Option<f64>. When serialized to JSON with serde, use #[serde(serialize_with = ...)] or ensure the field serializes as null not as absent. velocity_per_week requires at least 2 data points with different timestamps to compute a slope.
deliverables: velocity_per_week serializes as null (not absent) when Option is None
Velocity computation requires >= 2 prior snapshots

steps.name: JSON --trend flag outputs trend key with required top-level fields
steps.description: When invoked with --json --trend, the output JSON must contain a 'trend' object with at minimum: trend.snapshots (array), trend.schema_version (integer, value 1), and trend.direction (string: 'improving' | 'declining' | 'stable').
steps.criteria: Running barad-dur analyze . --json --trend produces JSON where: jq '.trend.schema_version' = 1, jq '.trend.direction' is one of 'improving'/'declining'/'stable', jq '.trend.snapshots' is an array.
quality_gates: All three required fields present and correctly typed
steps.implementation_notes: The JSON trend object is constructed in renderer/json.rs from TrendSummary. schema_version is a constant (1). direction uses Display of TrendDirection. snapshots maps SparklinePoint vec to [{timestamp, score}] array. The renderer receives Option<TrendSummary> and only injects the trend key when Some.
deliverables: trend.schema_version = 1 in JSON output
trend.direction string field present
trend.snapshots array present

steps.name: JSON --trend with 3+ prior entries includes delta and velocity fields
steps.description: When --json --trend is used with 3 or more prior entries in trends.json for the current branch, the trend object must include: trend.delta_vs_last (integer), trend.delta_vs_oldest (integer), and trend.velocity_per_week (number, not null).
steps.criteria: With 3 prior entries seeded in trends.json, running --json --trend produces JSON where jq '.trend.delta_vs_last' is an integer, jq '.trend.delta_vs_oldest' is an integer, and jq '.trend.velocity_per_week' is a number (not null).
quality_gates: All three fields numeric with 3+ prior entries
steps.implementation_notes: delta_vs_oldest compares current overall_score to the oldest same-branch entry in history. velocity_per_week is computed as (score_last - score_oldest) / weeks_elapsed, where weeks_elapsed = (last_timestamp - oldest_timestamp).num_weeks() as f64 (minimum 1.0 to avoid divide-by-zero).
deliverables: delta_vs_oldest computed in compute_trend
velocity_per_week numeric when >= 2 timestamps available
All three fields present in JSON trend object

steps.name: direction field is 'improving' when current score exceeds last score
steps.description: Verify that when the current overall_score is strictly greater than the most recent same-branch prior entry's overall_score, the trend.direction field in JSON output is the string 'improving'.
steps.criteria: Seeding trends.json with a prior entry of score 60 and running analyze with a mocked score of 65 produces JSON where jq '.trend.direction' = 'improving'.
steps.implementation_notes: TrendDirection::Improving is emitted when delta_vs_last > 0. Ensure the Display impl outputs lowercase 'improving'. This step validates the specific positive case; 03-07 validates the negative case.
deliverables: TrendDirection::Improving Display outputs 'improving'
compute_trend assigns Improving when delta_vs_last > 0

steps.name: direction field is 'declining' when current score is below last score
steps.description: Verify that when the current overall_score is strictly less than the most recent same-branch prior entry's overall_score, the trend.direction field in JSON output is the string 'declining'. Seed trends.json with a prior entry at score 99 to ensure the current run scores lower.
steps.criteria: Seeding trends.json with a prior entry of score 99 and running analyze on a repo that scores below 99 produces JSON where jq '.trend.direction' = 'declining'.
steps.implementation_notes: TrendDirection::Declining is emitted when delta_vs_last < 0. The seeded score of 99 ensures any real repo analysis will produce a declining result. The test constructs a fake trends.json in a tempdir with a single entry at score 99.
deliverables: TrendDirection::Declining Display outputs 'declining'
compute_trend assigns Declining when delta_vs_last < 0
